ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABZe_x0g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhDGLrU", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 37, "title": "Establish Firefox extension runtime with representative WebXR rendering and input", "body": "## Problem

Firefox runtime compatibility remains unverified. `build-firefox.ts` generates an MV3 event-page package, but `tests/browser-smoke.ts`, `tests/samples.ts` and `tests/wpt.ts` launch Chromium; panel control uses CDP. The earlier Playwright Firefox 157 attempt timed out at `about:debugging` before installation. Repeating that route or counting packaging as a runtime pass would not address the gap.

## Expected outcome

Provide a reproducible Firefox runtime/control route for the actual packaged extension, and working session, rendering, input and shutdown behavior across Quest VR, Quest MR and Android AR. Complete one pinned WebXR Sample and one pinned official Three.js example per profile. This is a useful prerequisite; the goal's additional application scenarios and unfinished modules remain outstanding.

## Context

Start from `dev` at `f9222484780d9993ce9202f3728c07ec00e6faea`. Relevant paths include `build-firefox.ts`, `manifest.json`, `src/extension/`, `src/app/panel.ts`, `src/types/contracts.ts` and the browser runners. Preserve the real MAIN/ISOLATED injection, event-page router, `cloneInto` bridge and inspected-tab ownership.

Mozilla documents [temporary unsigned BiDi installation](https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/remote/webdriver-bidi/Extensions.html#webextension-installparametersextension) and [web-ext temporary installation with a selected executable and fresh profile](https://extensionworkshop.com/documentation/develop/web-ext-command-reference/). These are candidate routes, not observed extension passes. Choose and pin a working browser/control combination; installation and genuine DevTools-panel control must both be demonstrated.

Use the pinned [Device CRD](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-webxr-20260609/), [AR CRD](https://www.w3.org/TR/2025/CRD-webxr-ar-module-1-20250425/), [Hit Test WD](https://www.w3.org/TR/2025/WD-webxr-hit-test-1-20251211/) and [Layers WD](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/WD-webxrlayers-1-20260811/).

Required application scenarios:

| Profile | Mode | WebXR Samples fb41c3416496974672e2c766a41c6febcba2d07e | Three.js r186, 9b4a2ac29c63ccb43fd51c5661f2f873ac2c39b8 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| quest-vr | immersive-vr | immersive-vr-session.html | webxr_xr_ballshooter.html |
| quest-mr | immersive-ar | hit-test.html | webxr_ar_hittest.html |
| android-ar | immersive-ar | hit-test.html | webxr_ar_hittest.html |

The Samples use base layers; normal Three.js capability detection selects projection layers. AR scenarios require `hit-test`. Three.js requests additional optional features: retain their actual negotiation rather than editing application requests. Ballshooter’s optional GPU depth does not require completing GPU depth in this Issue. Keep DOM Overlay Preview disabled for these baseline scenarios.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Add and document a focused Firefox runner command. Launch an explicitly selected Firefox executable in a fresh temporary profile, install the generated package, open its genuine WebXR DevTools panel and control the inspected tab. Record exact browser/build and driver/tool versions. Clean up processes, profiles and temporary installation on success and failure.
- [ ] Fix extension/runtime defects necessary for these scenarios. Exercise production injection, storage, routing and rendering; do not substitute a directly injected emulator, fabricated DevTools APIs or page-dispatched XR input events.
- [ ] Verify first-script `navigator.xr`/XR-global availability under the existing restrictive script-CSP fixture. Adapt the pinned WPT `navigator_xr_sameObject` assertion and identify its setup changes. Exercise the privileged bridge, an injected child frame and inspected-tab isolation.
- [ ] Verify inline support on both devices; Quest supports its selected immersive mode, and Android supports immersive AR. With activation supplied where required, unavailable modes and unsupported required features reject with `NotSupportedError`; unsupported optional features are omitted. A fresh immersive request without activation rejects with `SecurityError`.
- [ ] Run all six table entries with unchanged application/library source and normal capability exposure. Record source revisions and fetched dependency/asset provenance. Observation instrumentation may record behavior but must preserve arguments, results and exceptions; disclose it separately from upstream code.
- [ ] Each entry produces at least 30 XR animation callbacks and identifiable application pixels in the presented output. Check both positive-sized Quest eye regions and the Android mono view. AR transparent regions retain the virtual room. Callback counts or initialization alone do not satisfy rendering acceptance.
- [ ] Demonstrate application-visible input: panel-driven viewer/controller poses and firing in ballshooter; room hits, reticle rendering and select-driven placement in both AR applications. Android uses actual pointer interaction producing transient screen input; Quest uses tracked controllers. A focused fixture additionally checks select/squeeze sequencing and session-owned spaces/resources.
- [ ] Verify panel/page reload retains the selected configuration, an active profile/mode switch ends the prior presentation once, and explicit end permits restart without stale inputs or continued presentation. Test extension unload cleanup. Frames retained after dispatch cannot supply active-frame poses; foreign-session spaces fail with `InvalidStateError`.
- [ ] Run `npm run build:firefox` (including its existing typecheck/build), the focused Firefox command and `git diff --check`. If shared production behavior changes, run matching targeted Chromium regressions. Record failures, skips and unperformed checks; no extra generic suite rerun or independent AI re-review is required.
- [ ] Update installation instructions, runtime evidence and the capability inventory. Preserve historical failures and distinguish packaged, executed, working, failed and untested results. Keep remaining goal coverage explicit.

If an AI-authored requirement is technically mistaken, retain its original assumption, correction, pinned primary source and rationale in this Issue/PR. Make evidence-backed corrections without human approval or independent AI re-review; preserve meaningful acceptance instead of weakening it for unfinished implementation or failures.

## Optional validation

Additional pinned official application scenarios or Firefox versions, using the same runner. They do not block this bounded prerequisite.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. The Coordinator owns implementation, targeted execution, PR review and merge.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WebXR API compatibility goal for
Quest 3 VR/MR and Android AR. Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance
criteria when primary specifications or measured evidence establish the correction.
Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
